title: Returned-Payment Fee Posting on Home Comfort Financing Accounts
content:
**Servicing reference — Home Comfort Financing returned payments.**

Each returned payment is charged one returned-payment fee naming that payment, posted on the statement of the period in which the payment came back, on the first day after that period's statement closes or on the day the fee is fixed if later.

The returned-payment fee is fixed only after a replacement payment has posted for the returned installment or the installment's grace period has run out.

In terms of the account's records: the fee for a returned payment stands once the account shows a replacement payment posted for the returned installment, or once that installment's grace period has run out — whichever comes first; until one of the two holds, the fee is not fixed.

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| How many fees per returned payment | one, naming that payment |
| Statement it belongs to | the statement of the period in which the payment came back |
| Posting day | the first day after that period's statement closes, or the day the fee is fixed if that is later |

## Posting the fee: `post_returned_payment_fee_928f04f0`

**Capability.** `post_returned_payment_fee_928f04f0` posts the returned-payment fee for one payment that the borrower's bank returned unpaid on a Home Comfort Financing account. The fee line names the returned payment, appears on the statement month given as a returned-payment fee dated today, and the account balance rises by the fee. It books the amount supplied.

**How it is invoked.** Agent-side: the agent unlocks `post_returned_payment_fee_928f04f0` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `finance_account_id` | reference number of the financing account the fee is charged to, as shown by the financing account lookup for the verified borrower | identifier |
| `statement_period` | the statement month the fee belongs to | YYYY-MM (four-digit year, hyphen, two-digit month, e.g. 2026-04), in Eastern time |
| `source_txn_id` | reference number of the payment the bank returned — the payment line itself, not the returned-payment line — as shown in the account's transaction history | identifier |
| `amount` | the fee to post | USD, 2 decimal places, always positive, already rounded to the cent |

**Return.** The receipt carries `finance_txn_id` (reference number of the new fee line), `line_type` (always `returned_payment_fee`), `statement_period` (YYYY-MM month the fee was posted to), `source_txn_id` (the returned payment the fee names), `amount` (USD, 2 decimal places), `posted_date` (YYYY-MM-DD posting date), `account_balance` (USD, 2 decimal places, the balance owed after the fee) and `status`; "posted" means the fee is on the account.
